clue.text: Take a small tot to welcome new arrival?

definitions.text: Take a small tot to welcome new arrival?

parts.note: surface reading: give a little child a lift somewhere

parts.words: Take a small tot to welcome new arrival?
parts.note: setter's reading: a tot is also a small measure of spirits, drunk to toast a newborn

explanation.surface: Someone brings a toddler along to greet a new baby in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The tot looks like a child, but it is a small drink; the phrase is the British custom of drinking to celebrate a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the traditional celebratory drink taken by friends and the father after a baby is born.

clue.text: With gold medal at last, daughter set to be among the best

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of medal
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a class is a set or group

explanation.surface: Having finally won gold, a daughter is poised to rank with the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something world-class is of the highest standard internationally, among the very best.

clue.text: Doctor ran in last to change

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician who came last in a race wants to make a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation is a transformation from one form into another, and in geometry a shift of position.

clue.text: I can have Top Gear suspended

definitions.text: I can have Top Gear suspended

parts.note: surface reading: the BBC motoring programme being taken off air

parts.words: I can have Top Gear suspended
parts.note: setter's reading: top gear is headwear, which this furniture holds up on its pegs

explanation.surface: Someone claims the power to get the TV motoring show Top Gear taken off air.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC car show, but read literally it is clothing worn on top: hats, hung up on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is an upright pole with hooks for hanging headwear and coats.

clue.text: Celeb Lee personally carries electronic pagers

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A celebrity called Lee carries pagers about in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleepers is the British word for pagers, small devices that beep to summon someone.

clue.text: Batter in cold meal

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a spread of food from which guests serve themselves

explanation.surface: Batter served as part of a cold spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter looks like the cooking mixture, which fits the meal, but it is the verb meaning to pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to knock about, like waves or wind, and a buffet is a self-service cold spread.

clue.text: Observes short piercing tool go up and down

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: sees means observes
an awl is a tool for piercing holes in leather

explanation.surface: Someone watches a sharp tool bob up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move back and forth or up and down, like the playground plank.

clue.text: Put away odd letters ignored by tenants

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in place

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of tenants

explanation.surface: Peculiar letters addressed to the tenants are left unread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests storing things, but in informal speech it means to consume food.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an idiom for eating it, usually a lot of it.

clue.text: A great deal of traffic going over Devon river

indicators.note: going over means flipping, so the word is turned back to front
a great deal of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: traffic means trade, as in dealing in goods

explanation.surface: Heavy traffic crossing a bridge over a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic looks like cars, but it is the verb or noun for trading goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a river in Devon, flowing from Dartmoor to the sea at Dartmouth.

clue.text: Arrogantly claim bar must swap starters for meat dish

indicators.note: exchanging starters means the opening letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: to boast is to claim arrogantly
a reef is a bar of rock or sand in the sea

explanation.surface: A pub's bragging about its menu, with a nod to a classic Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a pub, but here it is a ridge of sand or rock under the sea; trading the two opening letters gives the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a classic British meat dish of oven-cooked joint of cattle.

clue.text: Put down teen posing before run

indicators.note: a person posing arranges themselves into a new position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A teenager is told off for showing off before going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests belittling, but here it means writing something down in a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record or write them down, as in a ledger or on a form.

clue.text: PC perhaps kept so busy at the end of day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of day

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police constable is kept busy right until the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable, but it is a personal computer; the jumbled letters come after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a computer designed to sit on a desk, and a PC is one example.

clue.text: Pass pasty around, pursued by first pair of seagulls

indicators.note: turning around makes the word read from the other end

parts.note: pasty describes a pale complexion

indicators.note: the first pair means the opening two letters are kept

parts.note: the opening two letters of seagulls

explanation.surface: Someone hands a pasty along while gulls swoop in after it at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Pasty looks like the Cornish pie, but it is the adjective for a washed-out complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes it is said to elapse; both verbs describe time going by.

clue.text: Device that picks up plate after you've stepped on it?

definitions.text: Device that picks up plate after you've stepped on it?

parts.words: picks up plate after you've stepped on it
parts.note: surface reading: someone retrieving a dish that was trodden on

parts.words: Device that picks up plate after you've stepped on it?
parts.note: setter's reading: a roadside device records a number plate after you step on the accelerator

explanation.surface: A gadget that collects a plate someone has trodden on.
explanation.walkthrough: Plate is a car's number plate, and 'step on it' is slang for accelerating.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside camera photographs the number plates of vehicles exceeding the limit.

clue.text: Relief after trial that audiologist provides?

indicators.note: one thing coming after another means it is placed second, behind the word that follows it in the clue

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court
aid means relief, help

explanation.surface: The relief felt once a court case is over.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiologist treats deafness and fits patients with small devices that amplify sound.

clue.text: Beginners note metres regularly introduced by nonsense poet

indicators.note: being introduced by something means it comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
N is the abbreviation for note

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one here

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of metres

explanation.surface: A lesson for novices on musical notes and poetic metre, led by a famous versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners and beginners are both people who are just starting out at something.

clue.text: Brazilian footballer's games with the French

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Brazilian star's matches played against France.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelé was the celebrated Brazilian forward who won three World Cups.

clue.text: Drop red case off close to luggage

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of luggage

explanation.surface: Leave a red suitcase beside the rest of the bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop ... off' reads as delivering luggage, but off is the anagram signal and Drop alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a fall in amount, and a decrease is likewise a reduction.

clue.text: Dazzling volume, and riotous playing

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for volume

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A band playing wildly and very loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso performance shows dazzling technical brilliance; here the word is used as an adjective.

clue.text: For example, Hearts match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four sets in a pack of cards
second meaning: to go well with or be appropriate

explanation.surface: Hearts, the football club, as an example of a team playing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts looks like the Edinburgh football club, which makes match seem like a fixture; both are card and verb senses instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four card suits, and to suit something is to go well with it.

clue.text: Get more excited for puzzle

parts.note: to get angry is to be angry, so get stands for be
wilder is the comparative of wild, meaning excited

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more and more agitated over a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder is to puzzle or confuse someone thoroughly; both are verbs.

clue.text: Repeat Spitting Image

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to do again, as in doubling back

explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV puppet satire show, so Repeat seems to mean a rerun of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To double is to repeat, and a person's double is their exact lookalike.

clue.text: One elitist's penned article about small tree cultivation

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so one piece is enclosed by the others
about means turned round, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article
a snob looks down on others

explanation.surface: A snob has written an article on growing miniature trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has: one elitist has penned the article, putting it between I and SNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing trees in miniature in pots.

clue.text: Pinto toppling fences completely

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the phrase holds the letters within it

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A piebald horse knocks over every fence on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinto is a horse with patchy colouring, which makes fences look like jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', meaning entirely or completely.

clue.text: Coach again on time ahead of wet weather

parts.note: re means on or concerning
T is the abbreviation for time
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A sports coach runs another session on schedule before the rain arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain someone is to teach or coach them a second time.

clue.text: Snappy type beginning to clear crumbs up

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of clear

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: crumbs and cor are both British exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A brisk sort starts sweeping up the crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumbs looks like breadcrumbs but is a mild British exclamation, as is cor.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is short for crocodile, an animal whose jaws snap shut.

clue.text: Backed by a bishop, that lady's returned for recovery treatment

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: her is the possessive of that lady
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: With a bishop's support, a woman comes back for treatment to get well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' means followed by: the reversed pronoun comes first, with A and the bishop behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, treatment to help a person recover, often from addiction.

clue.text: Having taken small spades out, shuts shed

indicators.note: taking things out means removing them, so those letters vanish from the word

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for spades in cards
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: After removing the little garden spades, someone locks the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades looks like garden tools, but it is the card suit, abbreviated like small.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut is a small simple building, much like a garden shed.

clue.text: Very long time devouring American Dad, television show

indicators.note: devouring something means swallowing it whole, so one part goes inside another

parts.note: so means very
A is the abbreviation for American
pop is an informal name for a father
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An American dad spends ages glued to the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very long time' reads as one phrase, but Very and long time are separate pieces, and it is the long time alone that does the devouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television or radio.

clue.text: How train reached Barking for Queen once

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters have gone haywire and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about how a train got to Barking, an east London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the place in east London, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Howard was Henry VIII's fifth wife and Queen of England until her execution in 1542.
